explanation: `var` is function-scoped, not block-scoped, so all three closures pushed inside the loop capture the exact same binding of `i`. By the time the returned functions are actually called, the loop has already finished and `i` equals 3, so every call returns 3 instead of the expected 0, 1, 2. Using `let` instead of `var` would give each iteration its own binding.
prompt: Why do all three calls below return 3 instead of 0, 1, 2?
choices: `var` makes all three closures share the same loop variable `i`, so by the time they're called it has already reached its final value of 3
`funcs.push` should be `funcs.unshift` to preserve the correct call order
The loop condition `i < 3` should be `i <= 3` to include the last index
Arrow functions must be used instead of anonymous functions for closures to capture variables correctly
